claims.text: As-cast HfNbTaTiZr is a single-phase BCC alloy with minimal pre-existing precipitates.
Aging HfNbTaTiZr at 600–800 °C promotes nucleation of nanoscale Ta- and/or Zr-rich precipitates.
Cold rolling introduces a dislocation network without altering the overall phase constitution.
The relevant precipitates form at grain boundaries or within grains and are enriched in Ta and/or Zr.
HfNbTaTiZr exhibits an unusual yield-strength plateau in the 873–1073 K range.
The alloy has distinctive, weakly temperature-dependent elastic behavior at elevated temperature.
The unusual stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior arises from a temperature-induced transition in dislocation dynamics.
The transition in dislocation dynamics is mediated by in situ formation of nanoscale Ta-/Zr-rich precipitates.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between the BCC matrix and precipitates generates local residual stresses.
The precipitates act as dynamic obstacles that pin dislocations.
Precipitate pinning shifts deformation toward an edge-dislocation-dominated mechanism involving thermally activated climb or super-jogging.
The combined residual-stress and dislocation-pinning effects stabilize yield strength and create the high-temperature plateau.
Residual stress fields caused by the precipitates alter and increase the effective elastic modulus.
Aged and modestly cold-worked specimens will have higher and more temperature-insensitive yield strength than as-cast specimens between 873 and 1073 K.
Aged and modestly cold-worked specimens will have a higher effective elastic modulus than the as-cast baseline.
Precipitate pinning will modify work-hardening behavior relative to the as-cast baseline.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr does not exhibit the yield-strength plateau or pronounced thermoelastic changes.
Precipitation and the associated dislocation mechanisms govern behavior from approximately 600 °C to 1073 K.
